decision_table.name: Determine_ID_Filing_Requirement
decision_table.description: Determine if corporation must file Idaho state corporate tax return. Checks for physical presence or doing business in Idaho.

condition.name: has_physical_presence
condition.comment: Has physical presence in ID (office, employees, property)

condition.name: has_economic_nexus
condition.comment: Meets ID economic nexus threshold or doing business standard

actions.action: // Physical nexus established - filing required // Apportionment will be calculated by tables 7000-7500

rule.policy:
ID filing required due to physical presence (office, employees, or property in state).
A corporation has physical presence nexus in ID if it has: - An office, store, warehouse, or other place of business in ID - Employees working in ID - Tangible personal property located in ID - Real property located in ID
Reference: Idaho Code § 63-3027 (Nexus and apportionment) Reference: Idaho State Tax Commission Corporate Tax Guidance Reference: Idaho Business Registration & Tax Nexus Rules

actions.action: // Doing business nexus or economic nexus established - filing required // Apportionment will be calculated by tables 7000-7500

rule.policy:
ID filing required due to doing business in Idaho or economic nexus.
Idaho uses a "doing business" standard for income tax nexus. Corporations establish nexus through: - Regular solicitation activities in Idaho - Deriving income from Idaho sources - Economic nexus threshold: $100,000 gross receipts
Activities establishing nexus include: - Maintaining employees or independent contractors in ID - Storing inventory within the state (including third-party fulfillment) - Trade shows, pop-up locations, or short-term assignments - Active solicitation resulting in Idaho sales
Federal Public Law 86-272 may provide protection for companies whose only Idaho activity involves soliciting orders for tangible personal property shipped from outside the state. However, this protection disappears when employees provide services, maintain inventory, or perform activities beyond pure sales solicitation.
Reference: Idaho Code § 63-3027 (Nexus requirements) Reference: Idaho State Tax Commission Economic Nexus Guidance Reference: Public Law 86-272 (federal protections)

No ID nexus - no filing requirement.
Corporation does not meet physical presence or doing business standards. Any estimated payments would be refunded.
Reference: Idaho Code § 63-3027 (Nexus requirements)

decision_table.name: Calculate_ID_Income_Adjustments
decision_table.description: Calculate ID state-specific additions and subtractions to federal taxable income.

condition.name: has_nexus
condition.comment: Must have nexus to calculate adjustments

rule.policy:
ID state-specific income adjustments to federal taxable income.
ID ADDITIONS to federal taxable income include: - State, municipal, and local taxes measured by net income - Expenses related to income not taxable under Internal Revenue Code - IRC Section 78 gross-up dividends (certain foreign tax situations) - Other additions required by Idaho Code § 63-3022
ID SUBTRACTIONS from federal taxable income include: - Interest and dividends not taxable under Internal Revenue Code (primarily U.S. government interest) - Interest on Idaho state and municipal bonds - Idaho net operating loss deduction (subject to Idaho limitations) - Dividend income exclusions (if applicable) - Other subtractions allowed by Idaho Code § 63-3022
Key difference from federal: Idaho does NOT tax interest on U.S. government obligations, while federal tax includes this income. This is a major subtraction item on Form 41.
Reference: Idaho Form 41 Lines 11-31 (Income Additions and Subtractions) Reference: Idaho Code § 63-3022 (Idaho taxable income defined) Reference: Idaho Form 41 Instructions

No nexus - no state adjustments calculated.
Corporation does not have ID nexus, so no income adjustments are needed.

decision_table.name: Calculate_ID_State_Tax
decision_table.description: Calculate ID state corporate income tax. Applies ID 5.3% flat rate to apportioned and adjusted taxable income.

condition.name: has_nexus
condition.comment: Must have nexus to owe tax

rule.policy:
ID state corporate income tax calculation:
1. Federal taxable income: [Form 1120 line 28] 2. Apportioned to ID: × [ID apportionment percentage] 3. ID additions: + [State taxes deducted, exempt income expenses, etc.] 4. ID subtractions: - [U.S. govt interest, ID municipal interest, ID NOL, etc.] 5. ID taxable income: = [Result] 6. ID tax rate: × 5.3% flat rate (effective 2025) 7. ID income tax: = [Tax before credits] 8. ID credits: - [Investment, R&D, broadband, new jobs, etc.] 9. ID tax liability: = [Final tax]
ID uses single-sales factor apportionment (100% sales factor).
ID tax rate history: - 2025+: 5.3% flat rate - 2024: 5.695% flat rate - Prior years: Progressive rates (phased out 2022-2024)
ID provides various tax credits including: - Investment tax credit (Idaho Code § 63-3029B) - Research and development credit (Idaho Code § 63-3029E) - Broadband equipment investment credit (Idaho Code § 63-3029G) - New jobs credit (Idaho Code § 63-3029I) - Small employer new jobs credit (Idaho Code § 63-3029J) - Community rehabilitation program credit (Idaho Code § 63-3029K)
Reference: Idaho Form 41 (Corporation Income Tax Return) Reference: Idaho Code § 63-3025 (Tax rate of 5.3%) Reference: Idaho Code § 63-3027 (Single-sales apportionment) Reference: Idaho State Tax Commission Corporate Tax Bulletin 2025

No ID nexus - no tax liability.
Corporation does not have physical presence or doing business nexus in ID. Any estimated payments are refunded.
Reference: Idaho Code § 63-3027 (Nexus requirements)

No ID taxable income - no tax liability.
Corporation has ID nexus but no positive taxable income after apportionment and adjustments. Any estimated payments are refunded.
ID net operating loss (NOL) rules may apply: - ID allows NOL carryforward for 20 years (as of 2025) - No carryback allowed (as of 2025) - NOL limited to 80% of taxable income (similar to federal)
Reference: Idaho Form 41 (Corporation Income Tax Return) Reference: Idaho Code § 63-3029 (Net operating loss deduction)
